reflections.title: "Your Refuge from the Avenger of Blood"

reflect.text: God told Israel to set apart cities of refuge within easy reach across the land. These towns provided a fair hearing and safe shelter for anyone who caused an accidental death. By giving this command, God showed how much He values human life. He built mercy directly into His law, making sure justice was handled with care and compassion.

The cities were placed so that anyone could reach one in less than a day. The community kept the roads clear and put up signposts pointing the way so that nothing would slow a runner down. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "the way to him is short." In the same way, we do not need to walk a complicated road of self-reliance to find safety. We simply turn from our own merit and trust Jesus, who welcomes us right away.

Whenever we face our mistakes, deep guilt, or painful troubles, God is our ultimate place of safety and our fair judge. The law also promised freedom to the runner when the high priest died. That pointed ahead to Jesus, our great High Priest, whose death pays for our sins and sets us completely free.

questions: What mistakes or heavy burdens do you need to take directly to God for shelter today?
Are there any ideas about your own goodness you need to leave behind to simply rest in Jesus?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for being our safe shelter when we are hurting, afraid, or weighed down by our faults. We thank You for Jesus, whose death took away our guilt and brought us freedom. Help us run straight to You whenever we are in trouble, trusting that Your door is always open. Amen.

reflections.title: A Safe Place for Everyone

reflect.text: God made sure these cities were open for all people, both the citizens of Israel and the foreigners living among them. Anyone who caused an unintended death could run to the city gates, speak to the leaders, and receive a home. They were given a place to live not only in safety from harm, but in quiet rest and peace.

This broad welcome looked forward to God opening the door of faith to everyone. God makes no difference between people of different backgrounds, for the same Lord generously blesses all who call on Him. Through the gospel, people from every nation share fully in God's promises, and Christ comes to live in our hearts as our living hope.

The gates of God's kindness stand open before us right now. Sometimes we hold back out of fear or hesitation instead of stepping in to enjoy what He has prepared. God invites anyone who is willing to come forward, enter His promises, and find lasting security in Him.

questions: Do you ever hesitate to step into God's promises, and what keeps you from entering fully?
How does knowing that God welcomes people from every background change how you view others?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, we thank You that Your mercy is wide enough for anyone who calls on Your name. Forgive us when we hold back or doubt that Your promises belong to us. Help us enter into Your peace with confidence and live each day resting in the shelter You provide. Amen.
